title: Stanford professors’ AI lab Noeri launches with $110m, backed by Nvidia
excerpt: ‘Every company we talk to is riding the same curve,’ says Carlos Guestrin, as his Stanford lab Noeri raises $110m with Nvidia’s backing.
content_html:
Noeri, an AI lab founded this year by Stanford professors Yejin Choi and Carlos Guestrin, has raised $110m, the company announced on Monday. Menlo Ventures led the round, with Madrona Venture Group, Kindred Ventures, Wing Venture Capital and NEA. Cisco Investments, Nvidia and Snowflake joined as strategic investors.

Bloomberg’s Dina Bass first reported the round earlier on Monday. Noeri did not disclose its valuation, Bloomberg reported.

What Noeri builds

Noeri builds self-improving AI for companies and for scientific research. It says most AI models stop learning once their training ends, while its systems keep improving on the job.

Its AI studies a company’s own data and workflows. It then changes the system around a task: the instructions, the tools, which model handles each step and, where it pays off, the models themselves. Each change comes with an explanation, and a person approves it, as in a code review.

The system works with closed and open-weight models. Customers keep ownership of their data and of the workflows and models they build, the company said.

Noeri also wants its AI to work with scientists. It would form hypotheses, run experiments and learn from the results, on problems from new molecules and proteins to complex technical systems. The company says smaller, specialised models make that kind of search affordable.

“Every company we talk to is riding the same curve: pay more for the best model, or settle for worse results from a cheaper one,” said Carlos Guestrin, co-founder and co-CEO of Noeri.

From a Stanford lab

Choi told Bloomberg the idea came partly from work with a Stanford microbiology and immunology team. The team wanted cheaper ways to use OpenAI’s models. Choi said their small AI, which learned to use other models, beat GPT-5 on that team’s research needs.

“We made this small AI that learns to use other AI, including GPT-4, but not 5 because at Stanford we are too poor to use GPT-5 all the time for research,” Choi told Bloomberg.

Choi and Guestrin are co-CEOs. Choi is a MacArthur Fellow and a former professor at the University of Washington and senior director at the Allen Institute for AI. Bloomberg reported that she was also a distinguished scientist at Nvidia.

Guestrin co-founded Turi, the machine learning platform Apple bought in 2016, and then led Apple’s central machine learning and AI organisation. He co-created XGBoost, an open-source machine learning library. Bloomberg describes him as director of the Stanford AI Lab.

Noeri has its headquarters in Palo Alto and an office in Zurich. It is hiring researchers and engineers in both cities. It is working with partners across industries, including some of its investors. Menlo Ventures also backed Town’s $108m round in October.

“Yejin and I both have worries about centralization, about one company owning everything,” Guestrin told Bloomberg.
